item.title: The philosophical case for feeling guilty about your Minecraft dog
item.description: A philosophy professor has killed three dogs in Minecraft and can't stop feeling bad about it. In an essay excerpted from his book How You Play the Game (2013), Huenemann describes the deaths with a bleak sense of comedy. The first two drowned after he built a bridge flush with the waterline — the dog got trapped underneath and let out "a single plaintive yelp before dying and sinking." — Read the rest The post The philosophical case for feeling guilty about your Minecraft dog appeared first on

item.title: The Met put 140 objects online as 3D models you can rotate
item.description: You can't see the back of a van Gogh painting at the Met. It's in a frame, against a wall. But the Metropolitan Museum of Art just put high-definition 3D scans of nearly 140 objects online, and now you can rotate "Wheat Field with Cypresses" to examine the brushstrokes from any angle, including the sides hidden by the frame. — Read the rest The post The Met put 140 objects online as 3D models you can rotate appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: The $30 billion AI code editor that might already be obsolete
item.description: Cursor's four cofounders became billionaires in 2025 selling an AI code editor that hit $1 billion in annualized revenue by November. Three months later, they held an all-hands meeting with slides titled "War Time." Over the holiday break, the company's own engineers had tested Anthropic's Opus 4.5 and found that the model could write code well enough to skip human review. — Read the rest The post The $30 billion AI code editor that might already be obsolete appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: International developers skipping GDC because the US no longer feels safe
item.description: For decades, the Game Developers Conference in San Francisco has been a yearly pilgrimage for game creators from around the world. This year, many are staying home. Developers tell Ars Technica they are increasingly unwilling to risk traveling to the United States amid stories of detentions, invasive searches, and political scrutiny at the border. — Read the rest The post International developers skipping GDC because the US no longer feels safe appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: Medical journal put a scientist's name on a fake paper, then demanded 499 euros to remove it
item.description: A journal put Laertis Ikonomou's name on a paper he never wrote, then tried to charge him 499 euros to take it down. Ikonomou teaches at the University of Buffalo. Last September, he found his name attached to a commentary in the Journal of Carcinogenesis & Mutagenesis, published by Walsh Medical Media. — Read the rest The post Medical journal put a scientist's name on a fake paper, then demanded 499 euros to remove it appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: Dead Kennedys' Jello Biafra hospitalized after hemorrhagic stroke
item.description: Jello Biafra, Dead Kennedys co-founder and Alternative Tentacles Records founder, suffered a hemorrhagic stroke on Saturday, March 7, caused by high blood pressure, according to a statement on the Alternative Tentacles website. He is hospitalized but stable. All appearances have been canceled. — Read the rest The post Dead Kennedys' Jello Biafra hospitalized after hemorrhagic stroke appeared first on Boing Boing.

item.title: Garden gnome fails to defend tiny patch of land against claim
item.description: Ownership of an 8ft by 3ft strip of land between two houses came into dispute after new owners moved in on one side. Though the patch had been lovingly tended by the other neighbors for years, after examining the plat the newcomers "decided the land was actually theirs," tore out the flowers growing there, and placed a garden gnome on it instead. — Read the rest The post Garden gnome fails to defend tiny patch of land against claim appeared first on Boing Boing.
